prompt: Build "Rubik's Cube", a single self-contained HTML file, three.js r160 only. A glossy, realistic 3x3 Rubik's cube in a dark studio with soft lighting and a subtle shadow or reflection. Standard colors. Layers must really rotate. 0-1.5s solved cube turning, 1.5-5s it scrambles itself with 20 seeded random turns, 5-14s it solves itself with every turn animated (any method allowed, including undoing the scramble), 14-15s a small celebration. Slow cinematic camera, no UI.

post.originalText:
All 4 Claude models solved a Rubik's cube. One of them cost over 100x more.

Same prompt, one shot, no edits: a glossy cube that scrambles itself, then solves itself.

Haiku 5.5: 7 min · $0.08
Sonnet 5.5: 7 min · $1.06
Opus 5.5: 13 min · $2.57
Fable 5.1: 25 min · $8.76

Plot twist: all four solved it the same way. They played the scramble backwards. The prompt allowed it.

Which cube wins? Reply 1, 2, 3 or 4

Prompt below, steal it:

Build "Rubik's Cube", a single self-contained HTML file, three.js r160 only. A glossy, realistic 3x3 Rubik's cube in a dark studio with soft lighting and a subtle shadow or reflection. Standard colors. Layers must really rotate. 0-1.5s solved cube turning, 1.5-5s it scrambles itself with 20 seeded random turns, 5-14s it solves itself with every turn animated (any method allowed, including undoing the scramble), 14-15s a small celebration. Slow cinematic camera, no UI.
